declared.description: The file's `run.access` and `run.reasoning.effort` as the engine reads them (the `access_requirement` receipt's keys); absent when the file declares neither

prompts_sent.description: This door holds no prompt: a session is opened, asked what it lists and ended

routes.description: One row per session shape the workflow's tasks run in and per model they resolve to: completion rows first, then agent rows

routes_omitted.description: Sessions the workflow names beyond the eight one request reads

status.description: read: the routes below were asked. not_applicable: the file selects no ACP sessions (no `run.access.via` under `run.access.protocol: acp`, or no `infer:`/`agent:` task with a static model); no session was opened and `reason` says why

current.description: The value the session holds now: what a run that declares none keeps on a session like this one

offered.description: The values, in the session's order. A run accepts a declared value only when it equals one of them exactly

status.description: offered: the session lists the option for the model. not_offered: it lists none. unobserved: not read, and `reason` says why (the model does not hold, the option is ambiguous or in another form, or no speed control is measured for this adapter release)

adapter.description: The adapter's own report on `initialize`; a value that is not a short graphic-ASCII token is absent

code.description: With unavailable: NIKA-1803 (adapter absent, silent or outside its pin), NIKA-1804 (session death) or NIKA-1805 (refused)

current.description: The native id the session holds (confirmed, legacy_list), its own model (session_default) or the one it answered instead (not_confirmed)

offered.description: The model values the session lists, in its order

omitted.description: Listed values not carried: beyond 64, or not a token

requested.description: The model as the file names it

status.description: confirmed: listed, selected for this session only and read back. session_default: the file names `default`. legacy_list: only the session's legacy model list names it, which answers no configuration. not_offered: the session does not list it. not_confirmed: listed, and the session answered another model. Efforts and tiers are read only under confirmed and session_default

observed_at.description: When this row was read. A row is served again until `fresh_until` (60 s after an observed reading, 15 s after an unavailable one)

profile.description: completion: the route's one-shot completion profile, which `infer:` tasks run under. agent: its agent session, which `agent:` tasks run in

reason.description: With unavailable: the engine's sentence, no path in it

status.description: observed: the session answered. unavailable: it gave no offer; `code` and `reason` say why, as a run on the route would meet it before its prompt

tasks.description: The tasks that resolve to this model in this shape

event_id.description: The id of that journal event

mime.description: The recorded media type, else one derived from the extension, else application/octet-stream

name.description: Unique within the job: `file/<path>` or `agent_image/<n>.<ext>` (the n-th image the job's agents sent that the blob store kept). The download route's `{name}`.

path.description: A file's project-relative path, as the workflow wrote it (normalized). Absent for an agent image.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the recorded bytes, as journaled

task.description: The task whose event records it

ArtifactManifest.description: A settled job's artifacts, as its sealed journal records them, bound to its receipt: `receipt` is the job's own (trace id and chain head included), `verdict` the tier its journal attained. At most 1024 entries are listed, in journal order; `truncated` says more exist (a download still finds every recorded name).

max_artifact_bytes.description: The largest artifact this server downloads (256 MiB by default)

CheckByName.description: Source-only Check by served name. Required launch inputs may remain unsupplied; caller inputs are accepted only on POST /v1/jobs and are refused here. Check does not execute an access plan.

access.description: Access pin, same vocabulary as `--access` (class or harness id). A pin never silently substitutes a metered seat.

CompileOutcome.description: The engine-owned machine document of one authoring result — the document `nika compile --json` prints, without the CLI-only `written`. No field grants authority, writes or executes source.

candidate.description: Ordinary `.nika` source. It is proposed only when `status` is `ready`; under any other status it is never proposed. Under `incomplete` it is a preview: it may still carry unfilled holes, or, when an `applied` diagnostic targets `verify_held`, it is a candidate the verifier held: it answered on these bytes against the request and did not accept them. A preview is not to be run or saved as an accepted result. Null when no candidate is shown, a withdrawn one included.

check_preview.description: The engine's pure Check report over the source only. No child file, skill, credential probe, access plan or admission was evaluated

diagnostics.description: Findings, in order. `kind` and `target` are their machine-readable part; `message` is for a reader. `target` names what a finding concerns: a question key, a task, a source field, or one of the compiler's own targets, among them `semantic_verification`, a finding on the request against the candidate's bytes (a clause or the whole request that no admitted judgment of these bytes settled, a part a verifier judged missing with its reason, a part it left unsettled or contested, a verification stopped at a judge call that got no answer); `verify_held` (kind `applied`), the candidate is held: the verifier answered on these bytes against the request and did not accept them (it rejected them or abstained), so `candidate` is a preview only, no replayable round is kept, and that verifier is not asked about the same bytes again in this round; and `verify_resume` (kind `applied`), no admitted judgment of the candidate was made (the verifier's call failed or chose no offered answer): the candidate is withdrawn and the round's record kept, and a zero-call replay of that round asks no verifier. Each verification attempt is recorded in `provenance.decision.semantic_verification`.

message.description: For a reader; never parsed to recover compiler state

provenance.description: Reproduction metadata; neither program identity nor run evidence

decision.description: Bounded compiler decision evidence, including deterministic and replay outcomes; it grants no execution or spending authority.

plan.description: The compiler record retained in this outcome; a server replay uses its opaque token rather than accepting this object as authority.

strategy.description: The compiler strategy that produced this outcome.

suggested_file.description: A suggested candidate file name, never a file written by compilation.

key.description: Stable semantic hole path such as `const.request`, never a session id

mandatory.description: false: the value belongs to a binding outside the program (a schedule's timezone, missed-run and overlap policies, per-run ceiling) and never blocks a ready candidate

options.description: Present on a choice question only: the admissible answers, keys spelled by the owning grammar

type.description: text: a JSON string · literal: one JSON value · choice: a JSON string that is the `key` of one of `options`

requested_boundary.description: The candidate's requested permits, derived by Check. Requested, never granted

requested_trigger.description: The trigger the request names (kind · source_hint · event_hint · cadence · at · payload_input · status · timezone · missed · overlap · ceiling · cron), stated beside the candidate whose bytes carry no cadence, host or event. A requirement the operator binds through the schedule contract, never a grant or a schedule row. timezone, missed, overlap and ceiling are the answered binding values (null until answered). cron is the exact five-field schedule projection when supported and fully specified, otherwise null; older engines omit it. It never supplies a missing time or timezone.

status.description: Completeness of authoring, never permission to execute

CompileRequest.description: Generation 1 of the compile request. The encoded body is limited by the listener's configured HTTP body ceiling; no smaller field-size or answer-count quota is imposed. Unknown fields, a present null, duplicate keys (including inside `answers`) and positional arrays are refused. No field names a host path: an EDIT base travels inline in `source`.

answers.description: Question key → one JSON literal with its type preserved, judged exactly as sent within the HTTP body envelope.

name.description: Bare constant name, not a path

value.description: One JSON literal, judged exactly as sent within the HTTP body envelope.

text.description: `Set const.NAME to JSON_LITERAL`, or `Set const.NAME` answered through `answers`

cognition.description: The only authoring cognition of this build. Any other value is refused; no authoring model is contacted

mode.description: create requires `intent` and forbids `source`/`change`; edit requires `source` and `change` and forbids `intent`

source.description: Accepted `.nika` source, inline. The caller owns source selection, revision checks and materialization

workflow_id.description: Names a created workflow. On edit the core refuses it as data: an edit cannot rename its accepted base

ExecutionSnapshot.description: Immutable byte-owned execution world — the body `nika check <file> --json --sdk-snapshot` prints (the engine is the one producer; a client never hashes). Unit bytes are canonical lowercase hexadecimal. `digest` and every unit `digest` are OPTIONAL caller-supplied integrity digests (canonical lowercase SHA-256 · a content assertion, never a signature): absent, the resident computes them and the receipt carries the result; present, they must match the bytes or the request is refused as `snapshot_tampered`. The decoded unit aggregate is limited to 16 MiB and the complete encoded request to 33 MiB. This object is the request body itself, not a path-bearing wrapper.

digest.description: Optional caller-supplied integrity digest of the world (never a signature)
Optional caller-supplied integrity digest of the unit (never a signature)

kind.description: 0 root (the admitted workflow) · 1 child (a transitively invoked workflow) · 2 skill (an Agent Skill document) · 3 import (an opaque import the caller supplied)

storeFormatVersion.description: Durable store formats this resident reads and writes; independent of the HTTP and event protocol versions.

outputs.description: Declared workflow outputs; present only after settlement when supplied by the execution adapter

ended_at.description: For an attempt queued again after losing its resident, when it was queued again.

execution_id.description: Absent on an attempt that waits and has not started.

mode.description: How this attempt was started again; absent on the first.

resumed_from.description: The trace this attempt continues, when it resumed the one before it.

spend.description: On an attempt that was started again: what the decision counted against the job's ceiling. `unknown` is present when some of it could not be read; it never counts for zero.

retry_state.description: `queued`: a new attempt waits in its owner's lane. `exhausted`: the job took its bound of attempts, so a request would be refused. `refused`: the resident decided not to start it again, and says why (`retry_reason`, and the code of the job's last event or error). `none`: nothing waits and nothing was refused, including a job whose latest attempt failed for a reason of its own while its bound leaves room. Open: a later engine may add a word.

JobByName.description: The by-name form (ADR-131): a workflow the served registry lists (GET /v1/workflows · project-root-relative, `.nika`). The resident captures its world exactly as a schedule does — the one owner of the snapshot and its digest domain. Idempotency binds to these request bytes. Optional `access` is the same pin as CLI `--access` (a pin is a pin). Absent: the resident's unpinned plan. Snapshot bodies reject both access and inputs overlays, including null or empty maps. Optional inputs are literal JSON values checked against declared keys, types and required values before a job exists; strings are never CLI @env instructions or expressions. Optional `owner` and `labels` (health capability `jobAttribution`) are what the caller states about the job so its application can find it again (GET /v1/jobs): they are attribution inside one authority domain, never an authorization boundary, and whoever holds the token reads every job. They bind the exact request identity like every other member; a snapshot body carries none, and a cost review binds none (they are stated on the admission that consumes it). Optional `retry` (health capability `jobRetry`, ADR-156) states whether the job is started again when its run loses its owner; it binds the request identity too.

access.description: Access pin, same vocabulary as `--access` (class or harness id). A pin never silently substitutes a metered seat.

inputs.description: Literal JSON overrides for declared workflow inputs. Unknown keys, wrong types and missing required values refuse with 422; defaults remain authored. A present null is refused. Inputs bind exact request identity and survive durable queue recovery; workflow bytes are unchanged.

labels.description: At most 16 caller labels. A key is 1 to 64 bytes of letters, digits and `._/-` (no colon); a value is at most 256 bytes of text without control characters. Outside these bounds, or null: 422 invalid_job_labels.

owner.description: Who the caller attributes this job to: opaque to the engine. Outside its bounds, or null: 422 invalid_job_owner. Require the `jobAttribution` capability first: a resident without it refuses the member as an unknown field.

retry.description: What the caller states about starting this job again when its run loses its owner: the resident stopped or was killed while the job ran (ADR-156). Stating it, even empty, is the caller's consent to run the workflow's effects a second time. Absent: the resident's own policy applies, and only to a workflow the engine classes as free of external effects. Unknown members, null, or a value outside its bounds: 422 invalid_job_retry. Refused on a request that consumes a cost review. Require the `jobRetry` capability first: a resident without it refuses the member as an unknown field.

max_attempts.description: The most attempts this job may take, counting the first. It lowers the resident's `--retry-max-attempts`, never raises it.

max_cost_usd.description: A ceiling for the re-attempts alone (USD). Stating it accepts that an attempt whose spend could not be read is followed by another; without it such a job stays `interrupted` (`unknown_spend`), whether or not a ceiling bounds the job. It never raises the ceiling that covers every attempt of the job.

on_interrupted.description: `resume` serves the tasks the interrupted attempt's journal completed and runs the rest, once the journal is judged as `nika run --resume` judges one; a journal that does not pass leaves the job `interrupted` (`resume_refused`). `restart` runs the whole workflow again as a new attempt of the same job, with its own execution and trace identity. `off` leaves the job `interrupted`. Absent: the resident's `--retry-interrupted`.

at.description: When the resident admitted the event (RFC 3339 · UTC). Outside the event's hash chain; absent on an event written before the journal was dated.

kind.description: The resident's event vocabulary: execution.<word> (queued · started · prepared · requeued · settled · cancelled · interrupted · refused · aborted_before_claim), plus the approval_decided frame the journal admits. Null on a payload that carries no kind.

JobList.description: One page of the job list, newest admission first. Open by contract: a later engine may add a member, and a client ignores the members it does not know.

next_cursor.description: Present while an older match exists: send it back as `cursor` with the same filters. Absent on the last page.

missed_count.description: How many slots that silence holds

missed_first.description: First slot of the silence a catch-up-once run answers for, on a catch_up firing only; scheduled_for is its last slot

schedule_id.description: Origin-local identifier, bounded to 255 UTF-8 bytes by the server

JobReceipt.description: Terminal binding to the exact immutable admitted execution

attempt.description: The attempt this request retries, the first being 1: the job's latest. Naming it makes the request safe to send again.

max_cost_usd.description: A ceiling for the re-attempts alone (USD), in force for the attempts after this one until another request states one. Stating it accepts that an attempt whose spend could not be read is followed by another. It never raises the ceiling that covers every attempt of the job.

mode.description: `restart` runs the captured workflow from its first task. `resume` serves the tasks the attempt's journal completed and runs the rest, once the journal is judged as `nika run --resume` judges one; the resident never falls back to `restart` on its own.

JobStatus.description: queued and running: the resident owns the execution. interrupted: execution ownership was lost and effect settlement is unknown — an EVIDENCE state (the journal is INCOMPLETE), never a run state (ADR-129). paused, succeeded, failed and cancelled: the run's own settlement, the words its terminal frame carries (ADR-128).

JobStatusOnly.description: Status only. Redacted diagnosis lives on GET /v1/jobs/{id} and SSE, never here.

JobSummary.description: What the list shows of one job. Open by contract, like `JobList`. It never carries inputs, outputs, a receipt or a settlement.

attempts.description: How many attempts the job took or holds, the first included (ADR-156); `GET /v1/jobs/{id}/attempts` lists them.

created_at.description: When the resident admitted the job (UTC). For a job admitted before the resident dated admissions: the date of its first dated event, or absent.

error.description: On a failed job only: the redacted diagnosis GET /v1/jobs/{id} carries.

labels.description: What the caller stated; empty on an unlabelled job.

owner.description: What the caller stated; absent on an unattributed job.

retry_state.description: `queued`: a new attempt waits in its owner's lane. `exhausted`: the job took its bound of attempts, so a request would be refused. `refused`: the resident decided not to start it again, and says why (`retry_reason`, and the code of the job's last event or error). `none`: nothing waits and nothing was refused, including a job whose latest attempt failed for a reason of its own while its bound leaves room. Open: a later engine may add a word.

workflow.description: The served workflow name captured at admission.

JournalEvidence.description: Reported journal delivery loss, independent of execution status. The reason classifies the mirror's first error without exposing OS text or paths. Absence is not a claim that a journal exists.

Occupancy.description: What the resident holds now against its limits. Open by contract: a later engine may add a member, and a client ignores the members it does not know.

max_concurrent.description: Jobs the resident runs at once.

max_concurrent_per_owner.description: Jobs one owner runs at once; null when unbounded. Its other jobs wait.

max_queued_per_owner.description: Jobs one owner may have waiting; null when unbounded. Past it an admission answers 429 `owner_queue_full`.

queue_capacity.description: Jobs that may wait, all owners together. Past it an admission answers 503 `queue_full`.

queued.description: Jobs admitted and waiting for a worker.

owners.description: The owners that hold a job now, busiest first.

owner.description: The stated owner; null for the jobs that state none, which share one lane.

owners_omitted.description: Owners that hold a job and are not named above.

providers.description: The providers the operator capped (`--provider-concurrency`), by id. A provider with no cap is not listed: the resident does not count its calls. Empty when none is capped.

in_flight.description: Calls that hold a slot now: sent and not yet answered.

max_concurrent.description: Model calls this provider may have in flight at once, all jobs together.

waiting.description: Calls that wait for a slot. They are sent in turn as slots free.

RunSettlement.description: The run's settlement (ADR-128), built once by the runtime and projected whole: the state word every door speaks, why, the elapsed time on the kernel clock, the task tally, the spend with its qualifier, the failure named. Unknown cost is never zero: `total_cost_usd` is absent when nothing was metered. Present on the terminal event and durable job response of a job whose runtime settled; absent when the resident lost the execution (interrupted) or refused it before any task. Reattachment and idempotent admission replay project the same hash-bound terminal event, never a new settlement.

task.description: The task that failed · absent for a run-level cause

total_cost_usd.description: Present only when at least one leaf metered real spend

stopped_calls.description: Every MCP call the run stopped waiting for, on every path (a task's timeout, an operator Stop, a task that continued or recovered after it): the task, the tool as the workflow names it, the call's id, and whether the call left. `unknown`: the call reached the server, which may have acted, so an effect's outcome is unknown; `not_sent`: it was stopped before it was sent. Absent when the run stopped no MCP call.

never_started.description: Cancelled at the boundary without ever starting (counted in `cancelled` too)

ok.description: A recovered task IS a success (counted here too)

ScheduleList.description: Every schedule the resident holds: API schedules by id, then project beats by id. Open by contract: a later engine may add a member.

truncated.description: True when the resident holds more schedules than one list answers.

inputs.description: Per-fire inputs bound on every resident fire (#1370): one scalar per key the workflow declares under `inputs:`, coerced by the declared type exactly as the CLI `--var` edge does, then judged by the same literal admission validator as POST /v1/jobs. Unknown keys, values the declared type refuses, missing required inputs and the `@env:` channel are refused at PUT and again at fire.

labels.description: The labels every job this schedule starts carries, under the law of `labels` on POST /v1/jobs. Part of the schedule revision only when stated.

owner.description: Health capability `scheduleManage`. Who the jobs this schedule starts are attributed to: every job it fires or a trigger admits carries it (GET /v1/jobs?owner=). The same law as `owner` on POST /v1/jobs: attribution inside one authority domain, never an authorization boundary. Part of the schedule revision only when stated, so a schedule that states none keeps its revision.

ScheduleStatus.description: Normalized definition, origin, distinct schedule revision, active/pause state, due verdict, bounded next slots with shift evidence, earliest wake hint, and last durable decision.

SnapshotValidationAck.description: Compact remote acknowledgement that the exact snapshot was revalidated. This is not the engine's public full check report; SDK callers retain the engine-owned report captured with the snapshot and return it only after this acknowledgement succeeds.

TraceVerification.description: Run-scoped verdict on the journal the resident wrote for the job, through the ONE verifier `nika trace verify --json` runs. `verdict` is the CLI's headline word: the attained tier (ok · sealed · anchored · replayed), incomplete for a journal with no terminal frame (the writer's liveness rides `reason`), tampered for a buried seal, broken for an edited chain, and the CLI's refusal classes; `unavailable` only when no journal exists for the job (refused before its first event · queued · a backend keeping none). `reason` is the machine class beside it (the seal tier under a ladder verdict). The CLI's own document rides verbatim (exit · chain · seal · anchor · replay · lines); a filesystem path is never returned.

chain.description: events · head · headline (intact · torn · incomplete) · liveness (alive · dead · unknown · null)

exit.description: The CLI's exit class: 0 the reported tier holds · 2 a forged or edited journal · 3 the environment (unchained · unreadable · a missing input) · 5 incomplete lifecycle evidence

lines.description: The CLI's ladder lines, the journal path replaced by <journal>

seal.description: tier (unsealed · sealed · forged · buried · unattributable) and the tier's facts

tier.description: The CLI's own `tier`, verbatim: the attained tier over an intact chain, or its refusal class. `verdict` is its projection; a forged seal still reads `ok` here with `exit` 2, so read `exit` and the legs, not a word alone.

bearerAuth.description: Exactly one Authorization: Bearer value from the token file

info.description: Authenticated loopback remote execution, declarative schedules, verified downloads of the artifacts a settled job's sealed journal records, and stateless source-only authoring (POST /v1/compile never runs, admits or writes). Schedule backfill, /v1/arm, and POST /v1/run are absent.
info.title: nika serve

get.description: Reads, without a prompt, what the sessions of the served workflow's own `run.access` route list for its models: the models, the reasoning efforts and the service tiers. The route and the models are the file's: a request names a served workflow and nothing else. Each session is opened as a run opens it and ended before any prompt. A row is an observation with a time, kept 60 s (15 s when unavailable) and served again meanwhile; one reading runs at a time. An offer authorizes nothing: POST /v1/jobs still selects, reads back and refuses on its own session. `{name}` is sent as for GET /v1/workflows/{name}. Advertised by `accessSessionOffer` on /health; an engine without the token answers 404.

parameters.description: The served name, `/` separators sent literally (it spans several path segments)
parameters.name: name

200.description: The offer document, also when the file selects no ACP sessions (status not_applicable) or a session gave no offer (a row with status unavailable)

get.summary: What the sessions of a workflow's declared ACP route offer now

post.description: Runs the same admission as POST /v1/jobs (ADR-131 · both forms) over the exact request body, and creates nothing.

200.description: Compact snapshot validation acknowledgement, not the full engine check report

404.description: No workflow by that name under the served registry (by-name form)

413.description: Encoded body or decoded snapshot resource limit

422.description: Malformed, unsupported, tampered, or semantically refused snapshot

post.summary: Judge a workflow without creating a job — by served name, or as immutable snapshot bytes

post.description: The HTTP transport of the same Compile core as `nika compile`. Foundation scope: CREATE resolves an exact embedded skeleton name (or `hello`), EDIT changes one existing constant, answers are explicit JSON literals; any other intent is answered `incomplete` with no substitute workflow. Creates no job, run, approval or trace, writes no file, contacts no provider: ambient keys are never consent. `check_preview` is a REVIEW of the source only, never admission: POST /v1/jobs judges a candidate again. Questions carry stable keys; answering is a new request, not a session.

200.description: Authoring outcome — ready, incomplete and refused are all data

413.description: Encoded body above the compile ceiling

500.description: Compiler machinery failure; nothing is echoed

503.description: compile_busy — every compile slot is in use

post.summary: Author a candidate workflow without running it (stateless · source-only)

get.description: Health capability `jobList`. One page of the jobs this resident keeps, newest admission first, as light summaries: a summary never carries inputs, outputs, a receipt or a settlement (read them on GET /v1/jobs/{id}). Every query member is optional and they combine with AND. The list is a view inside one authority domain: filtering by `owner` is never an authorization boundary, and whoever holds the token reads every job. Pages are stable: a job admitted while a caller pages is newer than every page still to come, so no summary repeats or is skipped; a job the resident stopped keeping simply no longer appears. An unknown member, a repeated single member or a value outside its bounds is refused, never ignored.

parameters.description: The exact owner the job's caller stated.
parameters.name: owner

parameters.description: Any of these statuses. Repeat the member or separate values with commas.
parameters.name: status

parameters.description: The exact served workflow name captured at admission.
parameters.name: workflow

parameters.description: `manual`: submitted through POST /v1/jobs. `schedule`: fired by a resident schedule.
parameters.name: origin

parameters.description: `key:value`, split on the first colon. Repeatable, at most 16; every pair must be a label of the job.
parameters.name: label

parameters.description: Admitted strictly after this RFC 3339 instant. Write a `+` offset as `%2B`. A job admitted before the resident dated admissions is placed by its first dated event, and left out of a dated listing when it has none.
parameters.name: created_after

parameters.description: Admitted strictly before this RFC 3339 instant.
parameters.name: created_before

parameters.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page, sent back unchanged with the same filters. Opaque: never build or parse one.
parameters.name: cursor

400.description: `invalid_job_query`: an unknown member, a repeated single member or a value outside its bounds · `invalid_job_cursor`: not a cursor this list wrote

post.description: Two forms, one admission (ADR-131). `{"workflow": "<name>"}` names a workflow the served registry lists: the resident captures its world through ExecutionService, exactly as a schedule does. Optional `access` on that form is CLI `--access` for this job only. A snapshot body is the world `nika check <file> --json --sdk-snapshot` prints, decoded and readmitted through the same ExecutionService; its digests are optional caller-supplied integrity digests (a content assertion, never a signature). Snapshot jobs inherit the resident's unpinned plan. The server never interprets a caller filesystem path. Idempotency binds to the exact request bytes. Waiting jobs are served fairly (health capability `occupancy`): the next free worker goes to the owner with the fewest jobs running, in turn among equals, first in first out inside one owner; jobs that state no owner share one lane. A resident may bound what one owner holds: past its waiting bound the admission answers 429 `owner_queue_full` with `Retry-After`, and past its running bound the owner's other jobs wait while free workers serve other owners.

404.description: No workflow by that name under the served registry (by-name form)

409.description: Idempotency key already bound to another request

413.description: Encoded body or decoded snapshot resource limit

422.description: Malformed, unsupported, tampered, or semantically refused snapshot

429.description: `owner_queue_full`: this owner already has as many jobs waiting as one owner may have. Nothing is written and the idempotency key stays unbound; other owners are still admitted. Retry the same request when one of the owner's jobs starts.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before the retry. A hint: the resident cannot know when one of the owner's jobs will start.

503.description: Execution queue or durable store unavailable

post.summary: Admit a workflow as a durable job — by served name, or as immutable snapshot bytes

get.description: Answers only for a settled job (succeeded, failed, cancelled, interrupted); an interrupted run never sealed its journal, so its job answers 409 `artifact_journal_unavailable`. The manifest is read from the journal the job's receipt names, judged by the one verifier `nika trace verify` runs: the chain must be intact, the seal must verify against a run key that verifier weighs on the server, in the order the server signs (the public half of an explicit `NIKA_RUN_KEY_FILE` · `NIKA_RUN_PUB_FILE` pair, `~/.nika/keys/run-signing.pub`, the retired-key ledger), and the head must be the receipt's `chain_head`. Each entry is one journal event that records a written byte stream with its SHA-256: a file a builtin saved (`nika:chart`, `nika:image_generate`, `nika:tts_generate`, `nika:image_fx`, `nika:image_compose`) at a relative path inside the project and outside its `.nika` (refused by name in any ASCII case, and by device and inode under any other spelling the filesystem folds onto it), its last write winning, or an image an agent's harness sent, kept under `.nika/blobs`. `nika:write` and `nika:edit` journal no hash of what they wrote, so their files are not listed. Every size and digest is the journal's; the download route checks the bytes against them. No filesystem path of the server is exposed.

200.description: The manifest, bound to the job's receipt

409.description: `job_not_settled`: queued, running or paused · `artifact_journal_unavailable`: no receipt chain head, or no journal by the job's identity · `artifact_journal_unverified`: the journal is not sealed and intact with the receipt's head

500.description: `internal_error`: the server could not read the journal

503.description: `store_busy`: durable job state unavailable · `artifact_capacity`: every artifact slot is busy

get.summary: The artifacts a settled job's sealed journal records

get.description: `{name}` is an entry's `name` from GET /v1/jobs/{id}/artifacts, never a filesystem path. Every name contains `/` (`file/out/report.pdf`, `agent_image/1.png`): send it with its `/` literal or percent-encoded (`%2F`), as one path parameter. The rest of the path is percent-decoded once and matched exactly against the manifest's names; an escape that is not two hexadecimal digits, bytes that are not UTF-8 or NUL match no entry. The server opens the recorded place below the project root it holds, refusing a symbolic link at any component, and reads every byte against the recorded size and SHA-256 before the response starts (409 `artifact_changed` on a mismatch), keeping the SHA-256 of each 256 KiB chunk. While the bytes stream, each chunk is read again and sent only if it hashes to the digest kept for it: every byte that leaves is a byte of the recorded file, and a file changed during the stream ends it before its `Content-Length`. A stream also ends short when the server stops or cannot read the file: retry a short body, and a file that really changed then answers 409 `artifact_changed`. The bound is `max_artifact_bytes`; a larger artifact stays listed and is refused 403. At most 4 journal verifications and pre-download hash passes run at once (`artifact_capacity` otherwise); a stream holds no slot once its bytes start, is bounded by the connection limit, and is not bounded by the request deadline.

parameters.description: An entry's manifest `name`; its `/` may be sent literally or as `%2F` (decoded once, matched exactly)
parameters.name: name

schema.description: The artifact's bytes; Content-Type is the manifest's `mime`

Nika-Artifact-Sha256.description: The recorded SHA-256 (lowercase hex), the manifest's `sha256`

404.description: `job_not_found`: unknown or foreign job id · `artifact_not_found`: no entry by that name

409.description: `job_not_settled` · `artifact_journal_unavailable` · `artifact_journal_unverified` (as the manifest) · `artifact_changed`: the bytes at the recorded place no longer match the record

500.description: `internal_error`: the server could not read the journal or the artifact

get.summary: Stream one artifact's bytes, verified against its journaled SHA-256

get.description: Health capability `jobRetry`. The policy in force for the job (the resident's `--retry-interrupted` and `--retry-max-attempts`, as the job's own `retry` narrows them), where it stands about being started again, and each attempt oldest first. An attempt that was started again keeps its identity, its receipt, how it ended and what the decision that closed it counted; the attempt in hand carries its spend in its own settlement on `GET /v1/jobs/{id}`. Each attempt has its own journal: `GET /v1/jobs/{id}/trace/verify?attempt=N` verifies one.
get.summary: Read every attempt of a job

post.description: A queued job cancels atomically before execution claims it. An active job receives the run-scoped cancellation signal and returns 202 until its execution owner settles: the result may be success, failure or cancellation. The grace is fixed at 5 seconds from the signal: a run that has not reached a wave boundary and settled by then is dropped and the job settles `interrupted`, never an invented cancellation. A task still inside one long step when the signal arrives (an agent turn, a long wait) typically outlasts the grace. A paused or final observation returns its existing result unchanged.

200.description: Cancelled before execution, or already ended observation

202.description: Cancellation requested; execution has not yet settled

post.summary: Request cancellation or replay an ended observation

200.description: text/event-stream; sends bounded retry guidance and cursor-neutral heartbeat comments; Last-Event-ID replays only persisted events after that sequence; terminal data adds declared outputs and receipt when available; failures add redacted {code,message}

post.description: Health capability `jobRetry`. The latest attempt of a job that ended `interrupted` or `failed`, and that its caller did not cancel, becomes evidence and a new attempt of the same job is queued, with its own execution and trace identity. The request is the caller's consent to run the workflow's effects again. The bound of attempts in force for the job, the one ceiling over every attempt and, for `resume`, the judgment of the attempt's journal hold as for a run that lost its owner (ADR-156). The place in the owner's lane is taken before anything is written. The same request sent again answers 200 with the job as it stands and writes nothing.

200.description: The same request already retried this attempt: the job as it stands. A job still `queued` is put back in its owner's lane unless it waits already

409.description: `job_not_retryable`: the job did not end `interrupted` or `failed`, a cancellation was accepted on it, its latest attempt never started, or `attempt` is not its latest · `retry_exhausted`: the job reached its bound of attempts · `resume_refused`: the attempt's journal cannot be resumed, or a schedule fired the job · `unknown_spend`: what an attempt spent cannot be read, and no `max_cost_usd` is stated · `budget_exhausted`: nothing is left under the job's ceiling

422.description: `invalid_job_retry`: the body is not a retry request

429.description: `owner_queue_full`: this owner already has as many jobs waiting as one owner may have. Nothing is written and the idempotency key stays unbound; other owners are still admitted. Retry the same request when one of the owner's jobs starts.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before the retry. A hint: the resident cannot know when one of the owner's jobs will start.

503.description: `store_busy`: durable job state unavailable · `queue_full`: the execution queue is at capacity · `stopping`: the resident is stopping

post.summary: Start the latest attempt of a settled job again

get.summary: Status only; diagnosis lives on GET /v1/jobs/{id} and SSE

get.description: Locates the journal the resident wrote for this job under the project it serves (by the job's execution and trace identity) and verifies it through the same verifier `nika trace verify` runs; the vocabulary is the CLI's. `unavailable` is the honest refusal when no journal exists. The response never exposes a filesystem path.

parameters.description: The attempt whose journal is verified (ADR-156); the latest when absent. Each attempt has its own journal, chain and seal.
parameters.name: attempt

400.description: `invalid_trace_query`: a query member other than one `attempt=N`

404.description: `job_not_found` · `attempt_not_found`: the job has not taken this attempt

get.description: Health capability `occupancy`. How many jobs run and wait now, the limits they are held to, the owners that hold the most, and the model calls in flight on each provider the operator capped. A point-in-time reading of this resident's memory, never a durable record: read GET /v1/jobs for the jobs themselves. Authenticated, unlike /health, because it names owners. At most 100 owners are named, busiest first; `owners_omitted` counts the rest.
get.summary: Read what the resident holds against its limits

get.description: Health capability `scheduleManage`. The schedules this door created, by id, then the beats the project's `nika.yaml` declares, by id. Each entry is the status GET /v1/schedules/{id} answers, planned now, with one next slot. A project beat is read here: GET /v1/schedules/{id} answers an API schedule, or a project beat that carries a finding. `truncated` is true when the resident holds more schedules than one list answers.

500.description: `schedule_store_corrupt`: durable schedule state failed integrity validation

get.summary: List the schedules this resident holds

delete.description: Health capability `scheduleManage`. Requires If-Match: the exact current ETag, or `*` for whichever revision is current. Removes the definition and its last-slot decision in one durable replacement; a schedule declared again under the same id starts with no history. A job the schedule already fired is untouched and settles on its own. A beat the project's `nika.yaml` declares is not this door's to remove and answers 409.

412.description: Precondition refused; carries the current revision

ETag.description: The current revision, when one exists

delete.summary: Remove one schedule this door created

put.description: Create requires If-None-Match: *. Update requires the exact ETag in If-Match. Identical lost-response retries are unchanged and retain the revision. A refused precondition answers 412 with the schedule's current revision (null when none exists). A definition the planner or the schedule validator refuses answers 422 with its findings; a malformed body, refused inputs or a refused workflow answer 422 with the error envelope.

412.description: Precondition refused; carries the current revision

ETag.description: The current revision, when one exists

422.description: Refused definition: its findings, or the error envelope

put.summary: Create or revision-conditionally update one resident schedule

post.description: Health capability `scheduleManage`. Admits ONE manual job that runs the schedule's workflow as it admits now, under the inputs, cost ceiling, owner and labels the schedule declares (the declared ceiling restricts the resident's, never widens it). The request carries no body, or an empty JSON object. The trigger consumes no slot and records no schedule decision: the cadence is unmoved and the next slot fires as planned. A paused schedule can be triggered: a pause holds the cadence, not the operator. The job's origin is `manual`; find it by the schedule's owner and labels. The `Idempotency-Key` binds to the schedule id: a retry under the same key answers the same job, even after the schedule changed, and the same key on another schedule or on POST /v1/jobs answers 409. This is an operator gesture behind the one bearer credential, never an inbound event door for a third party. A beat the project's `nika.yaml` declares is not this door's to trigger and answers 409.

409.description: `idempotency_conflict`: the key is bound to another request · `schedule_declared_by_project`: declared in the project file

422.description: `invalid_schedule_trigger`: the body is not empty · `schedule.workflow`, `schedule.workflow_outside_registry` or `schedule.inputs`: the schedule's workflow or inputs no longer admit

429.description: `owner_queue_full`: this owner already has as many jobs waiting as one owner may have. Nothing is written and the idempotency key stays unbound; other owners are still admitted. Retry the same request when one of the owner's jobs starts.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before the retry. A hint: the resident cannot know when one of the owner's jobs will start.

503.description: Execution queue or durable store unavailable

post.summary: Run one schedule now, as a manual job

200.description: Project-relative .nika names under the served registry (--workflows)

get.description: `{name}` is a served name exactly as GET /v1/workflows lists it: a project-relative path that usually contains `/` (`workflows/daily.nika`). Send its `/` separators literally, as path separators: GET /v1/workflows/workflows/daily.nika. A served name uses only ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-` and `/`, so no segment needs percent-encoding; an encoded separator (`%2F`) or any other escape is not decoded and answers 404.

parameters.description: The served name, `/` separators sent literally (it spans several path segments)
parameters.name: name
